# Wild walks in Orkney

Fancy a wild walk in Orkney? We've picked some of our favourite places to experience the elements.

- [Home](https://www.orkney.com/)
- [What's New](https://www.orkney.com/news)
- Wild walks in Orkney

- [0SCRAPBOOK](https://www.orkney.com/scrapbook)
- [0SHORTLIST](https://www.orkney.com/shortlist)

When wild weather hits, most people retreat indoors to a warm fire and a hot drink.

In Orkney, we’d always recommend taking a different approach. There is nothing quite like being on a beach or walking along a coastal path when the wind is blowing and the sea spray is splashing against your skin.

Here are our favourite spots for an autumn or winter wander, perfect for getting rid of the cobwebs and awakening the senses.

**Remember, if you're walking on Orkney's coastline, take extra care and never get too close to the edge.**

### Noup Head, Westray

[![Noup Head, Westray, Orkney](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12575/noup_head-_westray-_orkney.jpg)](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12575/noup_head-_westray-_orkney.jpg "View the gallery")

This is a special place to be all year round.

In the autumn and winter months you'll have waves booming off the cliffs below; during the summer there will be thousands of seabirds swirling above the sea. And [the beautiful lighthouse](https://www.orkney.com/listings/noup-head-lighthouse "Find out more about Noup Head Lighthouse") that marks the north-western tip of the Orkney archipelago is a constant presence.

[Hop on the ferry or plane](https://www.orkney.com/plan/getting-around "Find out more about getting around Orkney") from [Kirkwall](https://www.orkney.com/explore/kirkwall "Find out more about Kirkwall") and head to [Westray](https://www.orkney.com/explore/westray "Find out more about the island of Westray"), one of our largest islands. Visit this RSPB reserve and take the cliff-top paths for stunning views of natural arches and the lighthouse itself, built in 1898. [Follow our Noup Head Circular walking route](https://www.orkney.com/things/leisure/walking/noup-head-circular "View our Noup Head circular walking route") to make sure you don't miss a thing.

- [Warm up after your walk](https://www.orkney.com/news/wild-walks#)


There are some excellent options available in Westray if you want to find some shelter after your wild walk.



The [Pierowall Hotel](https://www.orkney.com/listings/pierowall-hotel "Find out more about the Pierowall Hotel"), [JACKS Chippy](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100063786961066 "Find JACKS Chippy on Facebook"), and [Saintear](https://www.orkney.com/listings/saintear "Find out more about Saintear") all offer meals, refreshments and takeaways. The Groatie Buckie café at [W. I. Rendall](https://www.facebook.com/wirendallshop "Find W. I. Rendall on Facebook") is a great place to visit for a quick cuppa or a light bite, as is the [Wheeling Steen Gallery](https://www.orkney.com/listings/wheeling-steen-gallery "Find out more about the Wheeling Steen Gallery"). If you're heading to the ferry terminal, the welcoming [Richan’s Retreat](https://www.orkney.com/listings/richans-retreat "Find out more about Richan's Retreat") offers small meals and hot drinks. Check opening times with all local businesses before travelling.


### Tresness, Sanday

[![Tresness, Sanday](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12579/tresness-_sanday-_orkney.jpg)](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12579/tresness-_sanday-_orkney.jpg "View the gallery")

[Sanday](https://www.orkney.com/explore/sanday "Find out more about the island of Sanday") is [famous for its beaches](https://www.orkney.com/explore/sanday/best-beaches-in-sanday "Find out more about Sanday's best beaches") and you'll find plenty of options here in autumn to help you get away from it all.

This beach, at [Tresness](https://www.orkney.com/listings/tresness "Find out more about Tresness in Sanday") on the east coast of the island, is one of the best. Wrap up warm and dodge the North Sea as it rolls ashore on the spotless sand.

The dunes provide perfect shelter too if you just want to sit back and listen to the sea and wind.

- [Warm up after your walk](https://www.orkney.com/news/wild-walks#)


There are plenty of options available in Sanday if you're looking for a cuppa after your walk.



The UK’s most northerly wood-fired pizzeria at [59 Degrees North](https://www.orkney.com/listings/59-degrees-north-cafe-pizzeria "Find out more about 59 Degrees North") offers delicious pizzas and a range of other homemade treats during the summer months and into early autumn. [The Belsair Hotel](https://www.facebook.com/belsairhotel "Find the Belsair Hotel on Facebook") serves up a range of tasty bar food. The [Sanday Community Craft Hub](https://www.orkney.com/listings/sanday-community-craft-hub "Find out more about the Sanday Community Craft Hub") also has a tearoom offering light bites, cakes, and teas and coffees. Check opening times with all local businesses before travelling.


### Yesnaby, West Mainland

[![Yesnaby Castle, Orkney](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12581/yesnaby_castle-_orkney.jpg)](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12581/yesnaby_castle-_orkney.jpg "View the gallery")

This is one of the most spectacular stretches of coastline in the islands. [Yesnaby](https://www.orkney.com/listings/yesnaby "Find out more about Yesnaby in Orkney") is found in-between [Stromness](https://www.orkney.com/explore/stromness "Find out more about Stromness") and [Skara Brae](https://www.orkney.com/listings/skara-brae-skaill-house "Find out more about Skara Brae") on the west coast of the mainland and should be on everyone's 'must see' list.

Head out on the path to the Brough of Bigging for mesmerising views north and south. During a westerly gale, expect huge waves crashing onto the cliffs and dark skies with rain clouds passing through. Further south you’ll pass rocky inlets full of sea foam before arriving at the Castle of Yesnaby, a fragile sea-stack.

Don’t venture too close to the edge at Yesnaby – just enjoy the sights and sounds from a safe distance.

- [Warm up after your walk](https://www.orkney.com/news/wild-walks#)


You won't be short of food and drink stops after visiting Yesnaby.



Just a short drive away, the [Skara Brae Visitor Centre](https://www.orkney.com/listings/skara-brae-skaill-house "Find out more about Skara Brae") cafe has a menu of meals, snacks, and refreshments. [The Orkney Brewery](https://www.orkney.com/listings/brewery-tasting "Find out more about the Orkney Brewery")'s Tasting Hall (open until October) is relatively close by and so is [The Orkney Dairy](https://www.orkney.com/listings/the-orkney-dairy "Find out more about the Orkney Dairy")'s Big Bun Box, which is full of cakes, milkshakes and more. Slightly further afield you'll find [Stromness](https://www.orkney.com/explore/stromness "Find out more about Stromness") and its range of shops and eateries. Check opening times with all local businesses before travelling.


### Dingieshowe, East Mainland

[![Dingieshowe, Orkney](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12583/dingieshowe-_orkney.jpg)](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12583/dingieshowe-_orkney.jpg "View the gallery")

If you're an early bird then a morning visit to [Dingieshowe](https://www.orkney.com/listings/dingieshowe "Find out more about Dingieshowe") in the [East Mainland](https://www.orkney.com/explore/east-mainland "Find out more about the East Mainland") is highly recommended.

Watch the low autumn or winter sun rise in the east, brightening up the sea and sand at this beautiful beach. There's also a good chance you'll be carefully watched by a seal or two in the surf.

Dingieshowe boasts an excellent nearby coastal walk too, so make sure you take the time to explore the area.

- [Warm up after your walk](https://www.orkney.com/news/wild-walks#)


After your Dingieshowe walk, you can head east to the [Deerness Distillery](https://www.orkney.com/listings/deerness-distillery-ltd "Find out more about the Deerness Distillery") to visit its cafe and visitor centre for a hot drink, light bite, or maybe even a gin tasting or two. Closer to Kirkwall is the excellent [Kirk Gallery & Cafe](https://www.orkney.com/listings/the-kirk-gallery-cafe-sheila-fleet-jewellery "Find out more about the Kirk Gallery & Cafe") at Sheila Fleet's base in Tankerness. Kirkwall Airport also has a cafe that's open to the public. [The Barrier View Cafe](https://www.orkney.com/listings/barrier-view-cafe "Find out more about the Barrier View Café") is a little further away but well worth a stop too. Check opening times with all local businesses before travelling.


### Hill of White Hamars, South Walls

[![Hill of White Hamars, Orkney](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12585/hill_of_white_hamars-_south_walls_orkney_com.jpg)](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12585/hill_of_white_hamars-_south_walls_orkney_com.jpg "View the gallery")

This spectacular stretch of coastline is relatively undiscovered, with most visitors to Hoy heading north to see the famous [Old Man of Hoy](https://www.orkney.com/listings/the-old-man-of-hoy "Find out more about the Old Man of Hoy").

Don't miss this [Scottish Wildlife Trust reserve](https://scottishwildlifetrust.org.uk/reserve/hill-of-white-hamars/ "Find out more about the Hill of White Hamars") though - it boasts cliffs, caves, sea-stacks, geos, natural arches and much more.

It’s a remote and wild place, and you’ll probably have it all to yourself. [Follow our walking route](https://www.orkney.com/things/leisure/walking/brims-to-longhope-coastal "View our Brims to Longhope walking route") to find out more.

- [Warm up after your walk](https://www.orkney.com/news/wild-walks#)


Hoy and South Walls are home to a few eating out options which are perfect after a coastal walk.



[The YM Longhope](https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100083383990403 "Find the YM Longhope on Facebook") runs a community café and Lunch Club on certain days during the week. The [Scapa Flow Museum](https://www.orkney.com/listings/scapa-flow-museum "Find out more about the Scapa Flow Museum") at Lyness has the popular Skalpaflòi Café with a menu full of lunch options, snacks, home bakes and refreshments. Check opening times with all local businesses before travelling.


### Marwick Head, West Mainland

[![Marwick Head, Orkney](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12587/marwick_head-_orkney.jpg)](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12587/marwick_head-_orkney.jpg "View the gallery")

These [huge 87-metre-high cliffs](https://www.orkney.com/listings/marwick-head "Find out more about Marwick Head") climb sharply out of the sea on the west coast of the Orkney mainland.

You can either walk to the top of the headland from the nearby Marwick Bay or take the shorter route from the small car park at Cumlaquoy. Either way, you'll be greeted with some of the finest coastal views in the islands.

There's plenty of history to be had here too, with the Kitchener and HMS Hampshire Memorial towering above the sea.

- [Warm up after your walk](https://www.orkney.com/news/wild-walks#)


Even one of the wildest locations in Orkney has some eating out options in its vicinity.



The [Orkney Brewery](https://www.orkney.com/listings/brewery-tasting "Find out more about the Orkney Brewery")'s Tasting Hall (open until October) is a short drive from Marwick Head, and in the opposite direction you'll find the [Birsay Bay Tearoom](https://www.orkney.com/listings/birsay-bay-tearoom "Find out more about the Birsay Bay Tearoom") with its range of meals, home bakes and hot drinks. Check opening times with all local businesses before travelling.


### Rackwick, Hoy

[![Rackwick, Orkney](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12589/rackwick-_orkney.jpg)](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12589/rackwick-_orkney.jpg "View the gallery")

This could possibly be the best place in Orkney to clear the head and connect with nature.

[Rackwick](https://www.orkney.com/listings/rackwick "Find out more about Rackwick") is an old crofting community tucked away on the west coast of [Hoy](https://www.orkney.com/explore/hoy-graemsay "Find out more about the island of Hoy"), at the end of a valley of glens and hills, with huge sandstone cliffs looming on either side. A rocky beach with a sliver of golden sand greets huge rolling waves during the autumn and winter months. You can walk here and back in a day, taking advantage of the passenger ferry from [Stromness](https://www.orkney.com/explore/stromness "Find out more about Stromness").

It’s a place you won’t forget in a hurry.

- [Warm up after your walk](https://www.orkney.com/news/wild-walks#)


Rackwick is about as remote as you can get in Orkney.



The only nearby option for food and drink is [the Beneth'ill Cafe](https://www.benethillcafe.co.uk/ "Visit the Beneth'ill Cafe website"), just a short walk from Moaness Pier. The cafe is open during the summer months when it offers light bites, burgers, home bakes, and hot and cold drinks. Check opening times with all local businesses before travelling.


### Brough of Birsay, West Mainland

[![Brough of Birsay, Orkney](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12591/brough_of_birsay-_orkney.jpg)](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12591/brough_of_birsay-_orkney.jpg "View the gallery")

This is a very unique place, even for Orkney. The tiny island is only accessible at low tide, when the sea retreats to reveal a concrete causeway, criss-crossing its way towards the shore.

[The whole coastline in the surrounding area is fascinating](https://www.orkney.com/things/leisure/walking/birsay-whalebone "View our Birsay Coastal walking route"), but a trip to the [Brough](https://www.orkney.com/listings/brough-of-birsay "Find out more about the Brough of Birsay") itself lets you explore the remains of Pictish and Norse settlements, with the west side of the island dropping off dramatically into the Atlantic.

Remember to check, double check, and triple check the tide times so you don’t get stuck. Contact the visitor centre at Skara Brae on [01856 841 815](tel:441856841815) for the latest times.

- [Warm up after your walk](https://www.orkney.com/news/wild-walks#)


You can sit and watch the tide come in at the nearby [Birsay Bay Tearoom](https://www.orkney.com/listings/birsay-bay-tearoom "Find out more about the Birsay Bay Tearoom") whilst enjoying its menu full of local ingredients, with burgers, quiches, sandwiches, home bakes and much more on offer. Check opening times with all local businesses before travelling.


### Windwick, South Ronaldsay

[![Windwick, Orkney](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12593/windwick-_orkney_orkney_com.jpg)](https://www.orkney.com/site/assets/files/12593/windwick-_orkney_orkney_com.jpg "View the gallery")

[Windwick](https://www.orkney.com/listings/windwick "Find out more about Windwick") is another quiet spot but it’s well worth taking a trip off the main tourist trail.

Visit in November and you’ll be greeted by the cries of hundreds of new-born grey seal pups on the rocky shore below. The area is part of a fantastic coastal route, stretching from the south of the island to the beach at [Eastside](https://www.orkney.com/listings/eastside "Find out more about the beach at Eastside") in the north.

Windwick also has its own sea-stacks and craggy coastline to enjoy.

- [Warm up after your walk](https://www.orkney.com/news/wild-walks#)


Head back to St Margaret's Hope for a couple of places offering sanctuary from an autumn or winter wander in Orkney.



[Robertson's Coffee Hoose](https://www.orkney.com/listings/robertsons-coffee-hoose-bar "Find out more about Robertson's Coffee Hoose") is a popular place for a hot drink and a bite to eat. Meanwhile, the [Murray Arms Hotel & Seafood Restaurant](https://www.orkney.com/listings/the-murray-arms-hotel-and-seafood-restaurant "Find out more about The Murray Arms Hotel & Seafood Restaurant") has an extensive range of the freshest Orkney food on offer. Check opening times with all local businesses before travelling.


* * *

**Remember, if you're walking on Orkney's coastline, take extra care and never get too close to the edge.**
